lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: precise definitions of angle, circle, line, and segment
lessonRef.title: Skill consolidation: precise definitions of angle, circle, line, and segment

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a perpendicular lines?
choices: two lines that never meet
two lines that form an isosceles triangle
two lines with opposite slopes
two lines that intersect to form right angles

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. Open the compass to more than half of AB. From A draw an arc above and below AB; from B, with the same opening, draw arcs crossing them. Draw the line through the two crossing points. What has been constructed?
choices: the perpendicular bisector of AB
the angle bisector of ∠A
a copy of segment AB
a line parallel to AB

items.prompt: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle of radius 7. What central angle does each side subtend?
Which statement correctly justifies the angle bisector construction?
choices: The ray drawn appears to split the angle evenly.
The construction builds two congruent triangles by SSS, so the angles at the vertex are congruent.
The construction relies on the angle being acute.
Equal arcs always produce equal angles regardless of the triangle.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a parallel lines?
choices: two lines with the same length
two coplanar lines that never intersect, however far they are extended
two lines that meet only at infinity
two lines the same distance apart at one point

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. From vertex V draw an arc crossing both rays at P and Q. From P and Q draw equal arcs meeting at R. Draw ray VR. What has been constructed?
choices: a line perpendicular to one ray
an equilateral triangle on PQ
the bisector of the angle at V
the perpendicular bisector of PQ only

items.prompt: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle of radius 3. What central angle does each side subtend?
Which statement correctly justifies the equilateral triangle construction on a given segment?
choices: The construction works only when the segment is horizontal.
The circles intersect, which guarantees 60° angles by definition.
The intersection point is the midpoint of the segment.
Both circles have radius equal to the segment, so all three sides are that same length.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a angle?
choices: a corner of a polygon
the amount of turn measured in degrees
the figure formed by two rays sharing a common endpoint
the space between two intersecting lines

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. Through point P not on line ℓ, copy the angle that a transversal makes with ℓ, placing the copy at P on the same transversal. What has been constructed?
choices: a line through P perpendicular to ℓ
the perpendicular bisector of the transversal
the reflection of ℓ across P
a line through P parallel to ℓ

items.prompt: A regular triangle is inscribed in a circle of radius 3. What central angle does each side subtend?
Which statement correctly justifies the perpendicular bisector construction?
choices: The compass width was more than half the segment, which forces perpendicularity.
Any line through the midpoint is a perpendicular bisector.
The arcs look symmetric, so the line must be perpendicular.
Both constructed points are equidistant from the endpoints, and the locus of such points is exactly the perpendicular bisector.
